A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoboSense dataset and benchmark. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and six-page supplements support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original RoboSense benchmark experiments for detection, tracking, motion forecasting, and occupancy prediction in Tables 4-7, with additional detection results in supplementary Table 9.

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark experiments and their outcomes in Tables 4-7 and supplementary Table 9.

M1.justification: The annotation pipelines, multimodal late fusion, tracking procedure, and BEVDepth adaptation for occupancy prediction remain unchanged, including the implementation described in Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same RoboSense collection, six scene categories, and six perception/prediction tasks. No dataset, domain, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 4-6 and supplementary Table 9 retain identical comparator membership, including the detection methods, AB3DMOT tracker, ViP3D, PnPNet, and simple motion baselines.

E3.justification: The split policy, sensor configurations, model/input settings, matching thresholds, forecasting horizon, and occupancy evaluation rules in Sections 4-5 and Appendix B are unchanged.

E4.justification: The sensor-layout and distance-range comparisons in Table 5, matching-function analysis in Figure 4 and Appendix B.4, and ICP illustration in Figure A2 are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statistical and uncertainty reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All nine tables retain their numerical entries, and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 6 reports PnPNet minADE of 0.89 m and EPA of 0.313 in both versions.

T1.justification: The matching criterion and metric equations in Section 4, coordinate transformations in Appendix A, and mathematical descriptions of label generation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about RoboSense's novelty, near-field annotation coverage, six benchmarks, and collision-point matching criterion.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning sensor complementarity, near-field occlusion and truncation, collision-point localization, and occupancy performance remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Sensor specifications, synchronization, preprocessing, backbone/input details, and supplementary annotation instructions are identical. The code/dataset link and stated data-access arrangements also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 42 references and research positioning. Changed citation back-reference page numbers reflect text reflow, not added or removed cited works.

P1.justification: The SJTU affiliation changes from 'School of AI and Department of CSE' to 'School of Computer Science'. The third contribution bullet corrects 'standarized' to 'standardized'; the narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 adds a robot logo to the main and supplementary title blocks and replaces Figure 3's robot artwork with a higher-resolution branded image, retaining its sensor labels. Minor spacing and page/column reflow occur; scientific plots and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The affiliation update, spelling correction, title logos, and Figure 3 artwork revision provide small administrative and cosmetic refinements. The scientific evidence, mathematical content, explanations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
